findings.title: User-ownership check skipped when no Integration row exists for the installation_id
findings.body:
When `Integration.objects.get(external_id=installation_id)` raises `DoesNotExist`, the view calls `pipeline.next_step()` straight away. The new `github_authenticated_user` vs. installer check never runs on this path.

`build_integration` then fetches the installation with the app JWT and creates the Integration for whatever `installation_id` was supplied in the query string. An attacker can therefore claim any GitHub installation of the app that has no Integration row yet. Examples:
- an installation whose webhook has not been processed yet (a race);
- an installation whose Sentry Integration was deleted while the app stayed installed on GitHub.

The security validation only covers the case where the webhook already created the row. The installer/permission check should also run on this path, e.g. by verifying the authenticated user can access the installation via `GET /user/installations` with the OAuth token.

findings.title: KeyError when Integration metadata has no 'sender'
findings.body:
`integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` assumes every existing Integration has a `sender` entry. `build_integration` only sets `sender` when `state.get("sender")` is present, and integrations created before this field existed (or through other paths) will not have it.

For those integrations this line raises `KeyError`, and the user gets a 500 instead of the error page. Use `.get("sender", {}).get("login")` and fail gracefully with `error(...)`.

findings.title: Unhandled exceptions from token exchange / user lookup cause 500s
findings.body:
`safe_urlopen(...)` sits outside the try block, so network or SSL errors propagate unhandled. `get_user_info(payload["access_token"])` raises (e.g. `IdentityNotValid`/`ApiError`) when GitHub rejects the token, and that is not caught either.

The PR description says these failure cases should render the "Invalid installation request" page. Instead they surface as server errors. Wrap both calls and return `error(request, self.active_organization)` on failure.

findings.title: OAuth authorize URL parameters are not URL-encoded
findings.body:
The authorize URL is built with an f-string that puts `client_id`, `state` and `redirect_uri` in without encoding. `redirect_uri` is an absolute URL containing `:` and `/`, and on some deployments it could contain `?`, `&` or other characters that break the query string.

Build the query with `urlencode({...})` so the redirect URI is always encoded correctly.

findings.title: OAuth state compared with non-constant-time equality
findings.body: The `state` CSRF token is compared to `pipeline.signature` with `!=`, which is not a constant-time comparison. The practical risk is low, but security token comparisons should use `constant_time_compare` (or `hmac.compare_digest`) to avoid timing side channels.

findings.title: test_installation_not_found no longer exercises the 404 path
findings.body:
The test now sends a deliberately wrong `state` (`ddd023...`), so it only checks the state-mismatch error from `OAuthLoginView`. It never reaches `build_integration`'s 404 handling ("The GitHub installation could not be found.").

Coverage for the installation-not-found behavior is silently lost. Use the correct state so the flow reaches the 404 branch, and keep the original assertion.
